prompt: Complete an immutable TemperatureReading class created through static factories ofCelsius, ofFahrenheit and ofKelvin, able to report itself back in any of the three scales.
explanation: Storing the temperature in a single canonical scale (Celsius) means every conversion is written once and every reading is automatically comparable, no matter which factory built it. The private constructor plus static factory methods let each entry point do its own conversion before handing a finished object back. Because the field is final and nothing mutates it, the object is immutable and safe to share.
hints: Pick one scale to store internally -- Celsius is the easiest -- and make every factory convert into it before calling the private constructor.
ofFahrenheit should apply (value - 32) * 5 / 9 before constructing; ofKelvin subtracts 273.15.
warmerThan can simply compare the two stored Celsius fields, because both objects were normalised on the way in. Use String.format(java.util.Locale.US, "%.1fC", ...) for toString.
